sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text:
Fercher, also remembered as Fercerini, was an Irish bard in the following of the generous
king Cú Roí, who had carried the woman Blathnat out of the Otherworld. She turned against him and
schemed with his rivals for his death. Loyal to the end, Ferchert took her under his arm and threw his
moment from a Munster precipice, and the steep kept both their lives.

okr.objective: Ferchertne follows his king across a cliff into death.
key_results: He served King Cu Roi as a loyal bard.
King Cu Roi took Blathnat from the Otherworld.
Blathnat plotted with his enemies, and the king died.
The faithful hero leapt from a Munster cliff and pulled her over with him.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
